description: Surface the REAL per-row provider build error in diagnostics and the picker, instead of the generic 'configured but no instance was built' message, and confirm/fix the Gemini-by-key build path. This is the primary fix and unblocks diagnosing the cloud-provider failures. It is entirely in the Rust core (providers + tauri-app crates). It has NO dependency on FEAT-002; they touch disjoint files (except the shared TS type additions, which live in FEAT-002). NOTE ON BASELINE: the offline sandbox cannot run cargo (crates.io 403); do not attempt `cargo build`/`cargo test`. Rely on tracing + fmt-check + structurally-correct tests; CI is the authoritative gate.
steps: In crates/providers/src/builtins.rs: add a new public function `list_available_models_with_build_errors(registry: &ProviderRegistry, configs: &[ProviderConfig], pricing: &PricingTable, build_errors: &std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String>) -> Result<AvailableModelsResult, ProviderError>`. Move the current body of `list_available_models` into it. In the branch where `registry.get(&cfg.id)` is None (the 'no instance was built' case), prefer a real captured build error: if `build_errors.get(&cfg.id)` is Some(msg), push a ProviderEnumerationError { provider_id: cfg.id.clone(), message: msg.clone() } (the REAL ProviderError Display captured at build time); otherwise fall back to the existing static generic message. Then make the existing `pub async fn list_available_models(registry, configs, pricing)` delegate to the new fn with an empty `&BTreeMap::new()`, preserving its current signature and behavior so the external callers (crates/providers/tests/demo_provider_extension.rs) and existing tests are unaffected.
In crates/providers/src/lib.rs: re-export the new `list_available_models_with_build_errors` alongside the existing `list_available_models` export.

In crates/providers/src/contract.rs: VERIFY (do not change unless leaking) that ProviderError's Display for every variant is display-safe. The Auth variant is `#[error("auth error: {0}")]` where {0} comes from SecretError::to_string() (NotFound(handle) or Backend(reason)) or the adapter's own reason string; confirm none of these carry resolved key material. Add a short unit test in contract.rs (or reuse an existing test module) asserting ProviderError::Auth("no secret found for handle 'gemini-cloud'".into()).to_string() contains the reason and NOT any key-shaped material.

In crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs `list_available_models_inner` (~line 467): replace the resilient build loop's `let _ = registry.build_from_config(cfg, state.secret_store.as_ref());` (~line 524) with a loop that captures the Err into a `let mut build_errors: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String> = BTreeMap::new();` keyed by `cfg.id` with value `err.to_string()` (the ProviderError Display). Keep building the successful rows (a per-row failure must remain non-fatal so Ollama and other healthy rows still build - do NOT regress the v0.7.3 non-fatal behavior). Then call the new `providers::list_available_models_with_build_errors(&registry, &configs, &pricing, &build_errors)` instead of the current `list_models(...)`. Add the needed import for the aliased new fn (mirror the existing `list_available_models as list_models` import style; e.g. import `list_available_models_with_build_errors`).

In crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs `provider_diagnostics_inner` (~line 641): apply the IDENTICAL change - capture per-row build Errs into a BTreeMap and pass it to `list_available_models_with_build_errors`. Because the diagnostics report is DERIVED from the shared enumeration result's `errors` (per-provider), the ProviderDiagnostic.error field will now automatically prefer the real build error for an unbuilt row. Keep `instance_built: registry.get(&cfg.id).is_some()` unchanged (a failed build => false + real error message). Keep the seeding/embedded-insert/derivation logic otherwise identical so the picker and diagnostics stay in lockstep.

Confirm the Gemini-by-key path builds end to end: trace build_gemini in crates/providers/src/adapters/gemini.rs - it requires cfg.api_key_ref (else ProviderError::Auth), resolves it via secrets.resolve (Auth on failure), defaults base_url to https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com when None, reads optional extra.project. set_cloud_provider_inner stores the key under id 'gemini-cloud' and persists ProviderConfig{ id:'gemini-cloud', kind:Gemini, base_url:None, api_key_ref:Some(ref-to-'gemini-cloud') }. Verify the api_key_ref handle written by set_cloud_provider equals the handle build_gemini resolves (both keyed by the config id 'gemini-cloud'), so a keyed Gemini row at default MUST build. If tracing reveals any mismatch (e.g. the stored SecretRef handle differs from what build_gemini looks up, or a required extra field is demanded), fix the wiring so a plain Gemini key builds and its list_models (GET {base_url}/v1beta/models with x-goog-api-key header) is reachable. Document the traced real cause in the feature findings.

Add/strengthen tests in crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs #[cfg(test)]: (a) STRENGTHEN `provider_diagnostics_inner_reports_unbuildable_row` (~line 3849) so that instead of only asserting the error is non-empty, it asserts the row's error is the REAL build error string (for the GenericOpenAI-with-no-base_url row that is the build_generic_openai message containing 'base_url', NOT the generic 'no instance was built' string). (b) Add a new test that persists a Gemini row (kind Gemini) whose api_key_ref points at a handle with NO stored secret (so resolve fails), driving provider_diagnostics_inner, and asserts that row reports instance_built == false with an error containing the real Auth reason (e.g. 'no secret found') and NOT the generic message - proving the Auth build failure is surfaced. (c) Add a test that a Gemini row WITH a stored key builds an instance (instance_built == true) via provider_diagnostics_inner (its list_models will error offline, which is fine and expected), proving a keyed Gemini row at default builds. Use the existing InMemorySecretStore-backed test_state() helper and ProviderRepo::new(state.session_manager.db()).insert pattern already used by the existing test.

Add a test in crates/providers/src/builtins.rs #[cfg(test)] asserting `list_available_models_with_build_errors` prefers a supplied build error over the generic message: register no instance for a config row, pass a build_errors map { row_id -> 'auth error: no secret found for handle X' }, and assert the returned errors vec carries THAT message for the row (and that the empty-map delegation path still yields the generic message).

Run `cargo fmt --manifest-path hybrid-orchestrator/crates/providers/Cargo.toml --check` and `cargo fmt --manifest-path hybrid-orchestrator/crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml --check` if a rustfmt binary is available offline; if fmt is not runnable, hand-verify formatting matches the surrounding code (4-space indent, trailing commas, flat-prose doc comments) and note it in findings.

Self-audit for clippy -D warnings: the removed `let _ =` now consumes the Result via `match`/`if let Err(e)` capturing into the BTreeMap, so there is no unused-Result warning; ensure no unused imports were left (the new import must be USED); no needless lifetimes introduced.
acceptance_criteria: providers::list_available_models retains its 3-arg signature and existing behavior; a new list_available_models_with_build_errors takes a &BTreeMap<String,String> of per-row build errors and, for an unbuilt row, surfaces the supplied real error in preference to the static generic message.

Both list_available_models_inner and provider_diagnostics_inner capture each build_from_config Err (keyed by cfg.id) and feed it to the shared enumeration, so a Gemini/generic build failure shows its REAL ProviderError message in the Diagnostics panel's `error` field (and the picker's enumeration errors) instead of 'provider is configured but no instance was built...'.

The v0.7.3 non-fatal behavior is preserved: a single failing provider build never aborts the whole enumeration; the auto-seeded Ollama row still builds and its single model still surfaces when Ollama is reachable.

A keyed Gemini row at default (base_url None) builds an instance (instance_built == true); a Gemini row whose secret cannot be resolved reports instance_built == false with the real Auth reason, not the generic message.
ProviderError Display remains display-safe (no key material) for all variants, asserted by a test.

New/changed Rust tests compile and are structurally correct (would fail if the code were reverted): the strengthened unbuildable-row test asserts the real base_url message; the Gemini tests assert the Auth-vs-built distinction; the builtins test asserts build-error preference.
verification: OFFLINE: cargo cannot run (crates.io 403). Verify by tracing and by reading the changed tests to confirm each asserts the new behavior and references the changed code path.
OFFLINE (if a rustfmt binary exists): `cargo fmt --manifest-path hybrid-orchestrator/crates/providers/Cargo.toml --check` and same for tauri-app.

CI (authoritative): the per-crate `cargo build/test/clippy --manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml` and `.../tauri-app/Cargo.toml` steps pass, including the new/strengthened tests, with clippy -D warnings clean.
findings:
IMPLEMENTED (Rust-only, providers + tauri-app).

ROOT CAUSE (traced): crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs built each provider row with `let _ = registry.build_from_config(cfg, secret_store);` in BOTH list_available_models_inner (~line 519) and provider_diagnostics_inner (~line 692), discarding the Err(ProviderError) that carries the real cause. The shared enumeration (crates/providers/src/builtins.rs) then had nothing but a static generic message to report for an unbuilt row (registry.get(&cfg.id) == None). So every failed cloud build showed 'provider is configured but no instance was built...'.

CHANGES:
- builtins.rs: added `pub async fn list_available_models_with_build_errors(registry, configs, pricing, build_errors: &BTreeMap<String,String>)` holding the full enumeration body; the unbuilt-row branch now prefers build_errors.get(&cfg.id) over the generic message. The existing 3-arg `list_available_models` delegates to it with `&BTreeMap::new()` (signature + behavior unchanged, so demo_provider_extension.rs and other callers are unaffected). BTreeMap was already imported.
- lib.rs: re-exported list_available_models_with_build_errors alongside list_available_models.
- commands.rs: both inner fns now capture each build_from_config Err into `let mut build_errors: BTreeMap<String,String>` keyed by cfg.id (value = err.to_string(), the display-safe ProviderError Display), keeping the build non-fatal (per-row failure leaves the row un-built, other rows still build => v0.7.3 non-fatal behavior preserved, seeded ollama-local still builds). Both then call list_models_with_build_errors (aliased import) instead of the 3-arg list_models. The routing caller at ~line 1615 still uses the 3-arg alias (routing only needs successful candidates), so both aliases remain used (no unused-import clippy warning). No `let _ =` remains.

GEMINI-BY-KEY (traced, wiring is CORRECT, no fix needed): set_cloud_provider_inner stores the key via `state.secret_store.store(id, api_key)` where id = cloud_provider_config_id(Gemini) = 'gemini-cloud', returning SecretRef('gemini-cloud'); it persists ProviderConfig{ id:'gemini-cloud', kind:Gemini, base_url:None, api_key_ref:Some(SecretRef('gemini-cloud')) }. build_gemini (adapters/gemini.rs) requires cfg.api_key_ref (else Auth), resolves THAT SAME handle via secrets.resolve (Auth on failure), and defaults base_url to https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com when None. The stored handle == the resolved handle, so a keyed Gemini row at default MUST build. THE REAL CAUSE the user hit (gemini-cloud 'no instance was built') was therefore a keyring resolve failure on their machine (SecretError::NotFound/Backend surfacing as ProviderError::Auth), which the discarded Err hid; surfacing it is the fix. The two generic-openai rows fail because GenericOpenAI has NO default base_url and the user pasted web/session URLs (that is FEAT-003's UX work); FEAT-001 now surfaces the real ProviderError::Other('genericOpenAI provider requires an explicit base_url ...') / Decode message for them.

SECRET HYGIENE VERIFIED: ProviderError Display is display-safe for every variant (contract.rs). Auth is `auth error: {0}` where {0} is SecretError Display (NotFound(handle)='no secret found for handle {0}', Backend(reason)) or an adapter reason string; none carry resolved key material. Added contract.rs test provider_error_auth_display_carries_reason_not_key_material.

TESTS ADDED/STRENGTHENED:
- builtins.rs: build_errors_are_preferred_over_the_generic_message (real error wins; empty-map delegation still yields generic).
- contract.rs: provider_error_auth_display_carries_reason_not_key_material.
- commands.rs: strengthened provider_diagnostics_inner_reports_unbuildable_row to assert the REAL base_url message and NOT the generic string; added provider_diagnostics_inner_surfaces_gemini_auth_failure (instance_built false + 'no secret found', not generic); added provider_diagnostics_inner_builds_keyed_gemini_row (instance_built true with stored key at default base_url).

VERIFICATION: offline sandbox INTEGRATIONS_ONLY, cargo build/test cannot run (crates.io 403). rustfmt IS available: `cargo fmt --manifest-path .../providers/Cargo.toml --check` and `.../tauri-app/Cargo.toml --check` both PASS clean after fixing one import wrap. Clippy self-audit: no `let _ =` discard left, both list_models aliases used, new import used, no needless lifetimes. CI is the authoritative gate.

NOTE: A live-steering message from the user about chat send-on-Enter/threading and a 'hello' to a local qwen3 ollama model getting no response is UNRELATED to FEAT-001 (frontend chat UX / streaming, not the provider-build-error surfacing in this Rust feature); left untouched here.
